CASE FILE // CLASSIFIED

Zero Trust lab

Keycloak and OpenZiti with tiered MFA and a deny-by-default firewall.

CloudKeycloakOpenZitiUFW2026

LAS Week 2

7

scenarios

roles, each with its own authentication tier

4

VMs in the VirtualBox lab

On this page01 // Setup02 // What I did03 // Results04 // What failed05 // Next

Setup

A four-VM VirtualBox lab with a Keycloak realm and three roles. Each role has its own authentication tier: password, password plus TOTP, and password plus TOTP plus passkey.

What I did

Keycloak is wired into OpenZiti as an external JWT signer, so access follows identity groups rather than IP addresses, with separate dial and bind policies per service.

Architecture

  1. Client identity password + TOTP + passkey
  2. Keycloak IdP
  3. OpenZiti controller + edge router
  4. App VM UFW deny-all

Results

UFW denies by default. The apps are reachable only through the Ziti overlay, and a direct SSH attempt by IP from the same subnet timed out.

Identity-based authorization (Keycloak JWT + OpenZiti) removes application port exposure from the network.

What failed

I documented a bind-policy misconfiguration that made clients act as service hosts instead of dialers.

Next

Audit the separation of dial and bind policies so clients are not misconfigured as service hosts.

Withheld on purpose: credentials , flags and lab IPs .
